core_obligations: Base of the induction: if the depth against the ideal is zero then the ideal lies in an associated prime, which then appears in the support of the quotient, so the dimension of that support is at least the dimension of the support of the module, and Cohen-Macaulayness makes the inequality an equality (proof lines 2072-2080)

Induction step: for positive depth choose an element of the ideal which is a nonzerodivisor on the module and note that dividing by it does not change the quotient by the ideal (proof lines 2083-2084)
Bookkeeping: the depth against the ideal and the dimension of the support both drop by exactly one, so the induction hypothesis applies to the quotient (proof lines 2085-2090)
proof_roadmap: 对 depth_I(M) 归纳。depth_I(M) = 0 时 I 含于某相伴素因子 p（ideal-nonzerodivisor）；p ∈ Supp(M/IM) ⇒ dim Supp(M/IM) ≥ dim(R/p) = dim Supp(M)（CM-ass-minimal-support 给等号）⇒ 结论。
depth_I(M) > 0 时取 x ∈ I 为 M 上非零因子；注意 (M/xM)/I(M/xM) = M/IM。
由 depth-drops-by-one：depth_I(M/xM) = depth_I(M) - 1；由 one-equation-module：dim Supp(M/xM) = dim Supp(M) - 1 ⇒ 归纳假设给出结论。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement computes the depth of a finite Cohen-Macaulay module with respect to a nontrivial ideal as the difference between the dimension of its support and the dimension of the support of the quotient by the ideal (author lemma at source lines 2060-2067, label lemma-depth-CM). The proof (source lines 2069-2091) runs an induction on the depth: in the zero case the ideal sits inside an associated prime which then supports the quotient, and Cohen-Macaulayness upgrades the resulting inequality to an equality; in the induction step a nonzerodivisor in the ideal is divided out, and both the depth and the dimension of the support drop by exactly one, which keeps the identity in step (proof lines 2083-2090). The induction and the base case are the substance. H3.
